content.comment_body: I recently bought a [product_name] to automate ventilation and lighting control. As a newcomer to [product_name], I found the product numbering system quite confusing. Looking at the product numbers for models with displays, there are versions like [article_no], and the ones with 'R' indicate relay types. This seems straightforward enough. Online discussions often refer to the [product_name] by the [article_no] version. At first glance, the device has a number printed on its housing ending with [article_no], and many shops list options ending with [article_no]. Based on a [company_name] datasheet from 2019, it appears [article_no] is the latest. However, when starting [product_name] programming software and selecting [article_no] as the hardware type, the number of inputs doesn't match expectations. It looks like [article_no] might be an older version. Upon using 'determine [product_name]', a list of possible types appears, with [product_name] [version_no] seeming most appropriate (is this a new numbering scheme?). My impression is that the current model actually corresponds to [article_no] (or perhaps [article_no] in hexadecimal)? Am I misunderstanding the numbering model, considering I haven't seen any reference to [article_no]? Also, how does this influence expansion modules? For instance, using two [article_no] expansion modules, they work as expected except for the RUN LED, which stays green even in stop mode. I hope someone can clarify this for me. Thanks, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. [company_name] last updated the names and order numbers of these devices at [article_no] series. There are now three generations of the [article_no] series: - The 1st generation appeared in September 2014 as the standard [article_no] in device selection, with order numbers like [article_no]. - The 2nd generation appeared in mid-2016, called [version_no], selectable as [version_no] in device selection, with order numbers like [article_no]. - The 3rd generation was released in December 2017, called [version_no], selectable as [version_no], with order numbers similar to [article_no]. There is no [product_name] with [article_no] or [article_no].

When the LED on an expansion module is green, it means the module is communicating with the neighboring device on its left. This is true regardless of whether the base module is in STOP or not. If the expansion module's LED is red, communication with the neighboring device is not happening. An orange/yellow LED indicates the module is in its initialization phase.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are confused by the [company_name] product numbering system for [product_name] and its expansion modules. Multiple naming schemes and generations create ambiguity, and mismatches between product documentation, module identification, and software options reduce user confidence and complicate setup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a transparent, unified numbering scheme that consistently matches device labels, datasheets, online information, and configuration software. Clear device identification and easy-to-understand module status feedback are expected.
